content:
# 1 Maccabees Chapter 15 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Verses:** 41 | **Disagreements:** 28

---

## Summary
Chapter 15 features two embedded documents (Antiochus's letter vv.2-9; Rome's circular letter vv.16-21) and the diplomatically significant exchange about land rights (vv.33-35). Disagreements concentrate on political/diplomatic vocabulary and Simon's land claim speech.

---

## Disagreements

**v.1** — "from the islands of the sea" — all agree; Antiochus was based in Rhodes or a similar Aegean island.

**v.3** — "certain pestilent men" (EMET) vs. "certain troublemakers" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "Traitors" (PNEUMA) — SOPHIA: "troublemakers" per established ruling on ἄνδρες λοιμοί.

**v.4** — "lay waste many cities" (EMET) vs. "devastated many cities" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.6** — "coin money for your country with your own stamp" (EMET) vs. "mint your own coinage for your country" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "mint your own currency" (PNEUMA)

**v.8** — "from this time and forever, let these be released for you" (EMET) vs. "from this moment and forever, let all of it be released to you" (LOGOS) — minor structural difference.

**v.9** — "your glory will be known throughout the earth" (EMET) vs. "your glory may be proclaimed throughout the earth" (LOGOS) vs. "your fame will spread throughout the world" (PNEUMA)

**v.10** — PNEUMA converts regnal year to "138 BCE"; others preserve regnal year.
- "all the forces joined him" (EMET) vs. "all the forces rallied to him" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.12** — "troubles had come upon him" (EMET) vs. "trouble had closed in on him" (PNEUMA) vs. "trouble had overtaken him" (LOGOS/SOPHIA)
- "his forces had left him" (EMET) vs. "his army had deserted him" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "his army had abandoned him" (PNEUMA)

**v.14** — "he pressed the city hard from land and sea" — all agree.
- "let no one enter or leave" (EMET) vs. "allowed no one to enter or leave" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "nothing in, nothing out" (PNEUMA)

**v.16** — "Lucius consul of the Romans" — all agree; this is L. Caecilius Metellus (or possibly Lucius Calpurnius Piso), 142 BCE.

**v.17** — "our friends and allies" — all agree.
- "to renew the ancient friendship and alliance" — all agree.

**v.19** — "not plot against them or fight against them" (EMET) vs. "not harm them or make war against them" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "do not attack the Jews, do not make war against them" (PNEUMA)

**v.21** — "pestilent men" (EMET) vs. "treacherous men" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "traitors" (PNEUMA) — parallel to ch.10 v.61 ruling; SOPHIA: "treacherous men."

**v.23** — Country list: all four translators preserve the full list verbatim without abridgment. Agreement.

**v.25** — "besieged Dor the second time" — all agree; this is the second siege mentioned.
- "continually bringing his forces against it" (EMET) vs. "continually pressing his forces against it" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "assault after assault" (PNEUMA)

**v.27** — "refused to accept them" — all agree.
- "annulled all the agreements that had been made with him previously" (EMET) vs. "repudiated all the agreements previously made with Simon" (LOGOS) vs. "threw out all the previous agreements" (PNEUMA) vs. "annulled all the agreements previously made with Simon" (SOPHIA)

**v.28** — "to negotiate with him" (EMET) vs. "to deal with Simon" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "to deliver an ultimatum" (PNEUMA — interprets the tone)

**v.29** — "Their borders you have devastated" (EMET) vs. "You have devastated their territories" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "You have ravaged the surrounding regions" (PNEUMA)

**v.31** — "give five hundred talents of silver for the destruction...and five hundred talents more for the tribute" (EMET) vs. "pay a thousand talents...five hundred for destruction and five hundred in back tribute" (PNEUMA calculates the total) vs. "five hundred...and another five hundred" (LOGOS/SOPHIA)

**v.32** — "the cupboard with gold and silver vessels" (EMET) vs. "the sideboard with vessels of gold and silver" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "a sideboard loaded with gold and silver vessels" (PNEUMA)
- "his great retinue" (EMET) vs. "his magnificent retinue" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) vs. "his large retinue" (SOPHIA — avoids interpretive adjective)

**v.33** — "We have not taken foreign land nor have we seized foreign property" — all four agree on this key verse.
- "which for a time was unjustly held by our enemies" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "which our enemies had unjustly held for a time" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) — word order only.

**v.35** — "we will give you a hundred talents for them" — all agree; significant that Simon offers 100, not the demanded 500.

**v.36** — "returned in anger" (EMET/LOGOS) vs. "walked out in a fury" (PNEUMA) vs. "returned to the king in anger" (SOPHIA)
- "the king was greatly angry" (EMET) vs. "the king was furious" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) vs. "the king was greatly enraged" (SOPHIA)

**v.38** — "governor of the seacoast" (EMET) vs. "governor of the coastal region" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "governor of the coastal region" (PNEUMA)

**v.39** — "to build Kidron and to fortify the gates" (EMET) vs. "to build up Kidron, to fortify its gates" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "fortify Kidron" (PNEUMA abbreviates)

**v.40** — "began to provoke the people" — all agree; PNEUMA adds "campaign of provocation."
- "to take people captive and to kill them" (EMET) vs. "to seize and kill the people" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "killing and kidnapping civilians" (PNEUMA)

**v.41** — "make forays along the roads of Judea" (EMET) vs. "make sorties along the roads of Judea" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) — "sorties" (military term) preferred over "forays."
